excerpt: Netlify builds, deploys and hosts websites and web apps. Credit-based plans from free to $20 a month, what the credits buy, and how it compares with Vercel and Cloudflare Pages.
content:
Netlify is a platform for building, deploying and hosting websites and web apps. You can start a project from a Git push, the command line, drag and drop, an API call or an AI prompt, and every route leads to the same project. Around the hosting it adds serverless functions for APIs, edge logic, scheduled and background jobs, instant databases and file storage, built-in identity, form handling, an AI Gateway for calling AI models, and Agent Runners that let AI coding agents such as Claude and Codex work on a site. Every change gets a deploy preview, and you can roll back in one click.

The company was founded in the summer of 2014 by Matt Biilmann, its CEO, and Christian Bach, its chief strategy and creative officer. It is headquartered in San Francisco with a distributed team. Netlify's About page says it has raised about $212 million, including a $105 million Series D in 2021 and a $53 million Series C in 2020, from investors such as Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins, Bessemer Venture Partners, EQT Ventures and Menlo Ventures. Its homepage claims more than 10 million developers, more than 60 million apps deployed and 99.99% uptime, and shows logos including Meta, Autodesk, Figma, Riot Games and Stack Overflow.

Credit-based pricing

Netlify now prices everything in credits. Each plan includes a monthly allowance, and usage draws it down: a production deploy costs 15 credits, compute 10 credits per GB-hour, bandwidth 20 credits per GB and web requests 2 credits per 10,000. AI inference varies by model. The Free plan has a 300-credit limit and includes deploy previews, custom domains with SSL, functions, storage, a basic firewall and the global CDN. Personal costs $9 a month with 1,000 credits; Pro costs $20 a month with 3,000 credits and unlimited team members. Extra credits come in packs: 500 for $5 on Personal and 1,500 for $10 on Pro. At the Pro pack rate Netlify works out a deploy at about $0.10 and a gigabyte of bandwidth at about $0.13. Enterprise has custom pricing, a 99.99% SLA, SSO and 24/7 support.

We have not tested Netlify ourselves. This page brings together Netlify's official site, its own announcements and reputable news coverage, plus the public pages of the products it is compared with, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.summary_short: Build, deploy and host websites and web apps, with functions, storage and AI features

team.name: Christian Bach
team.role: Co-founder, Chief Strategy and Creative Officer

gallery.alt: Netlify graphic reading 'Push your ideas to the web', with a browser window surrounded by icons for storage, images, commerce, AI and analytics
Netlify Pricing banner on a blue background with a 'Learn more' button

use_cases: Host a static or framework-based website deployed from Git
Share a deploy preview of every change before it goes live
Add serverless functions, forms and storage without running a server
Publish a site generated by an AI coding tool
Let AI agents work on a site through Agent Runners

fit: are a developer or small team shipping websites and front-end apps from Git
want previews, rollbacks, functions and forms without managing servers
like a free plan for side projects
not_fit: expect heavy bandwidth on the free plan: 300 credits covers about 15 GB of bandwidth and nothing else
need predictable fixed costs at scale: usage beyond the allowance is bought in credit packs
run long-lived back-end services or large databases; Netlify is built around front-ends and serverless functions

pros: Generous feature set on the free plan, including deploy previews and custom domains
Pro includes unlimited team members for one price
Clear published credit costs for deploys, compute, bandwidth and requests
cons: Credit maths takes some work to forecast
SSO and the 99.99% SLA are Enterprise-only

pricing.intro: Netlify's own plans, in US dollars. All plans are credit-based.

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: 300-credit limit; deploy previews, custom domains with SSL, functions, AI models, database, blob storage, basic firewall, global CDN

plans.name: Personal
plans.detail: 1,000 credits; secret detection, 1-day observability, priority email support

plans.name: Pro
plans.detail: 3,000 credits; unlimited members, private organisation repos, shared environment variables, 3+ concurrent builds, 30-day analytics

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: 99.99% SLA, enterprise network tier, high-performance builds, SSO and SCIM, log drains, 24/7 dedicated support

notes: Credit costs: production deploy 15; compute 10 per GB-hour; bandwidth 20 per GB; web requests 2 per 10,000; AI inference varies by model.
Credit packs: 500 for $5 (Personal), 1,500 for $10 (Pro), with auto-recharge.

alternatives.intro: Other platforms for deploying websites and web apps. Descriptions come from each product's own site; check their pricing pages for current rates.

items.name: Vercel
items.what: Cloud infrastructure it describes as the autonomous stack for every app and agent
items.difference: The most direct rival for deploying front-end and full-stack web apps.

items.name: Cloudflare Pages
items.what: Serverless full-stack platform for building and deploying applications on Cloudflare's network
items.difference: Runs on Cloudflare's own network and ties into Workers and its other services.

items.name: Render
items.what: Cloud for deploying and scaling apps and agents
items.difference: Better suited to long-running back-end services and databases as well as front-ends.
